# Foreword

This textbook accompanies the course "Basics of image processing" given in the second year of [master IRIV](https://www.master-iriv.fr/),
at the [University of Strasbourg](https://www.unistra.fr/).
The goal of this course, and consequently this textbook, is to give an overview of the main problems, tools and methods
encountered in digital image processing, from a practical point of view.
Therefore several examples and problems are given through programming exercices, gathered in section "Labs".

We choose to organize this textbook by sections, each one focus on a specific tool or problem.
In consequence, the number of sections may appear to be great, but this is counterbalanced by the fact that the sections are quite short,
therefore easy to read.
In addition to this, a section "In a nutshell" gives some explanation of tools that are used in image processing bu not specific to the domain,
so we put them apart and are not too detailed.

This course comes with [this Moodle page](https://moodle3.unistra.fr/course/view.php?id=13708) (accessible only to my students).

The programming exercices are with Python which is free and now used by many communities (medicine, astronomy, biology...).
To make the exercises on your personal computer, you must install Python and Jupyter Lab, as explained on page {ref}`C:python`.

For my french-spoken students, the section {ref}`C:glossary` list the french translation of the technical terms used in the textbook.

This textbook is written with [Jupyter Book](https://jupyterbook.org/) to be accessible everywhere from a computer, tablet or phone.
Nevertheless, it can be downloaded or printed.
To do that, save it to PDF by clicking on the icon <i class="fas fa-download"></i> on the top-right corner of the page.
